notes: Start with the governance decision: approve the reset now and shift the conversation from diagnosis to weekly execution. Point to the three owner-led workstreams and ask leadership to review one scoreboard every week until the gap closes.
title: Leadership should approve the H2 commercial reset now and run a weekly recovery cadence against the three levers that determine year-end performance

sections.heading: Decide now on the operating reset
sections.body: H1 already established the fact pattern: the business is behind plan on new bookings and renewals, while the underlying delivery base remains stable enough to support recovery. The leadership decision is therefore not another root-cause review; it is whether to impose a tighter commercial system immediately. Approving the H2 reset now creates one plan, one cadence, and one set of owners against the specific levers that control the remaining year-end outcome.

sections.heading: Manage the recovery through three owner-led levers
sections.body: The recovery plan should be run through three tightly defined workstreams, each with a single accountable leader. First, renewal management must prioritize at-risk cohorts, deal saves, and close-date control. Second, pipeline conversion must focus on late-stage progression and enterprise deal velocity, where the largest controllable bookings leakage sits. Third, pricing and packaging discipline must reduce avoidable discounting and sharpen offer quality so conversion improves without relying on broad volume expansion.

sections.heading: Use one weekly scoreboard to force intervention early
sections.body: Leadership should review a single weekly recovery scoreboard rather than a broad pack of lagging metrics. The scoreboard needs to show, by owner and by week, renewal saves, upcoming renewals at risk, late-stage pipeline movement, stalled enterprise deals, pricing exceptions, and committed actions due before the next review. This keeps attention on leading indicators of recovery, exposes slippage early, and turns the H2 plan from a target into an operating routine.

sections.heading: Hold owners to a fixed escalation path until year end
sections.body: The reset only works if missed commitments trigger action in the same week. Each workstream therefore needs explicit escalation rules: which accounts move to executive intervention, which deals require pricing approval, which stalled opportunities need unblock decisions, and which risks roll up to the leadership team. That discipline is the real ask on this slide. Year-end recovery depends less on new strategy than on management consistency, speed of intervention, and visible accountability every week.
